auth.subtitle: Sign in to manage your library.

library.title: Library
library.emptyHint: <add>Add a movie</add> or <scan>scan an existing library</scan>.
library.loadError: The library could not be loaded.

addMovie.noRootFolder: No root folder yet. <link>Add one</link> before adding a movie.
addMovie.searchOnAddHint: The indexers are queried in the background once the movie is added and the best release is grabbed.

movie.confirmDelete: Delete “{{title}}” and all its versions? Files stay on disk.
movie.confirmExclude: Also exclude this movie from future automatic additions?
movie.deleteFiles: Also delete the files from disk
movie.deleteFilesHint: The movie folder goes to the recycle bin when one is configured in Settings → Media management, otherwise it is deleted for good.

versions.title: Versions
versions.confirmDelete: Delete version “{{name}}”? The file stays on disk.
versions.noManagedCandidate: No other managed version can become the default.
versions.name: Name
versions.modeOneShot: One shot: downloaded once, never upgraded
versions.confirmDeleteFile: Delete the file of version “{{name}}”? It goes to the recycle bin when one is configured, and the version becomes missing again.

settings.removeFailed: The root folder could not be removed.
settings.addFailed: The root folder could not be added.
settings.scanHint: The scan is read-only: one top-level folder is one movie, one video file is one version on the “Any” profile, unmonitored. Nothing is moved or renamed.
settings.unmappedEmpty: None. Everything scanned found its movie.
settings.unmappedHint: Import by hand moves the files into a movie already in the library; add the movie first if it is not there yet.

pathPicker.browseHint: The folders below are the ones Bigarr can see, on the machine it runs on.

indexers.title: Indexers
indexers.hint: Torznab indexers are the ones Prowlarr or Jackett expose: point one at a Prowlarr indexer with its API key. The mock indexer fabricates releases for any film and is meant for development.
indexers.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? History and blocklist entries keep its name.
indexers.removeFailed: The indexer could not be deleted.
indexers.empty: No indexers yet. Add one to search for releases.
indexers.name: Name
indexers.mockHint: Fabricates a realistic list of releases for whatever film you search, including a few that must be rejected. No network, no download.
indexers.urlHint: Scheme and host of the Torznab endpoint, e.g. http://prowlarr:9696/1 — the API path is added.
indexers.categoriesHint: Newznab category ids, comma separated. Defaults to every Movies category.
indexers.priorityHint: 1 is highest, 50 lowest. Breaks ties between equal releases.
indexers.rateLimitHint: Minimum delay between two requests. Failures add an escalating pause on top.
indexers.testOk: Indexer reachable: {{categories}} categories, {{releases}} recent releases, id search: {{ids}}.
indexers.prowlarrManaged: Imported from Prowlarr: name, URL, key, priority and enabled state are refreshed on every sync. Categories, seeders, rate limit and seed criteria are yours.
indexers.prowlarrSynced: Prowlarr sync done: {{added}} added, {{updated}} updated, {{removed}} removed, {{skipped}} skipped.

search.title: Interactive search
search.hint: Queries every indexer once and shows every release with the reasons it is or is not acceptable for the selected version.
search.summary: {{releases}} releases from {{indexers}} indexer(s), {{approved}} acceptable for this version.
search.grabHint: Grab sends the release to the download client for the selected version; a rejected release can still be grabbed on purpose.
search.grabBlocked: This version already has an active download
search.autoSearchHint: Search the indexers and grab the best release for this version
search.autoNoIndexer: {{label}}: no indexer has automatic search enabled.

rss.title: Releases
rss.hint: Every release the RSS feeds bring in is matched to the library and judged by each version of the film. The first pass runs a minute after startup.
rss.synced: RSS pass done: {{fetched}} releases, {{new}} new, {{matched}} matched, {{grabbed}} grabbed.
rss.emptyMatched: No release matched a film of the library yet.
rss.grabHint: Each pass sends the best attributed release of every version to a download client. A release attributed but not grabbed lost to a better one of the same pass, or was refused by the client.

quality.title: Quality
quality.profilesHint: A profile ranks qualities (the order is the rank), sets the cutoff where a version is complete, and scores custom formats. A version follows one profile.
quality.name: Name
quality.languageHint: ISO 639-1 code (en, fr…). Bazarr reads it.
quality.cutoffHint: Quality at which a version is complete; above it nothing is fetched unless the custom format score is below the cutoff score.
quality.upgradeAllowed: Upgrade a file when a better release appears
quality.minFormatScoreHint: Releases scoring below are never wanted.
quality.cutoffFormatScoreHint: With the quality cutoff met and this score reached, nothing more is fetched.
quality.minUpgradeFormatScore: Minimum score gain for an upgrade
quality.minUpgradeFormatScoreHint: At equal quality a release must gain at least this much to replace the file.
quality.qualitiesHint: Best at the top. Ticked qualities are wanted; grouped ones rank together.
quality.formatScoresHint: Zero means the format is ignored by this profile. Formats are created or imported in Settings → Custom formats.
quality.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Versions using it must be moved first.
quality.definitionsHint: Sizes in MB per minute of runtime. A release outside the range is rejected; leave max empty for no limit.
quality.saveFailed: The change could not be saved.

customFormats.title: Custom formats
customFormats.hint: A custom format recognises a trait of a release: a group, a codec, HDR, a language, a size… Each quality profile gives it a score, positive to prefer, negative to avoid. Build one by hand or paste JSON.
customFormats.importHint: Paste a Radarr export or guide files (TRaSH and the like), one format or an array. A format already present, same guide id or else same name, is updated. Scores are left for you to set.
customFormats.testFailed: The title could not be evaluated.
customFormats.noneMatched: No custom format matches this title.
customFormats.testLanguageHint: The film’s original language (ISO code): a release naming no language is assumed to speak it.
customFormats.name: Name
customFormats.applySuggested: Apply the score the guide file suggests, {{score}}
customFormats.scoreFailed: The score could not be saved.
customFormats.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Profile scores and version constraints referring to it are removed.
customFormats.deleteFailed: The custom format could not be deleted.
customFormats.empty: No custom formats yet. Create one, or import JSON from a Radarr export or a guide.
customFormats.thresholdsHint: Minimum score, cutoff score and upgrade gain are set on each quality profile.

editor.name: Name
editor.includeWhenRenaming: Use this format in file names
editor.conditionsHint: Conditions of the same type: one must match. Conditions of different types: all must match. A required condition must always match.
editor.scoresHint: One score per quality profile. Zero: the profile ignores this format.
editor.jsonHint: Radarr’s shape: what you write here can go to Radarr and back.
editor.jsonInvalid: This JSON is not a custom format: {{message}}

downloadClients.title: Download clients
downloadClients.hint: Grabs are sent to the enabled client with the lowest priority number. Every torrent Bigarr adds carries the category below; the queue is what the client holds in that category. Downloads and libraries must share one mount for imports to hardlink.
downloadClients.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Its downloads stay in the client; Bigarr stops following them.
downloadClients.removeFailed: The download client could not be deleted.
downloadClients.empty: No download client yet. Add one to grab releases.
downloadClients.name: Name
downloadClients.mockHint: Downloads complete on their own after a minute and a half, without any network. Meant to exercise the queue.
downloadClients.hostHint: Host name or address of the WebUI, without scheme or port.
downloadClients.passwordHint: Leave both empty when the WebUI has authentication disabled for this address.
downloadClients.categoryHint: Created in qBittorrent if missing. Keep one category per Bigarr instance.
downloadClients.priorityHint: 1 is tried first when several clients are enabled.

queue.title: Queue
queue.liveHint: Connected to the server stream: the table updates after every poll of the download clients.
queue.pollingHint: The stream is down; the table refreshes every 10 seconds instead.
queue.noClients: No download client is enabled. Add one in Settings → Download clients.
queue.removeFailed: The download could not be removed.
queue.removeFromClient: Also remove the torrent from the download client
queue.removeFromClientHint: Unchecked, the torrent keeps running in the client and Bigarr just stops following it.
queue.deleteFilesHint: What the client has written so far. Nothing in the library is touched.
queue.blocklistHint: The release is refused for this version from now on. Use it for a fake or a broken torrent, not for a slow one.
queue.retryImportFailed: The import could not be retried.

rename.title: Rename files
rename.hint: Applies the current file name template of Settings → Media management to the files of this movie and to the extra files imported with them. Nothing else moves.
rename.nothing: Every file already matches the template.

history.title: History
history.loadError: The history could not be loaded.

manualImport.title: Manual import
manualImport.hint: Pick the movie and the version for each file. The import is forced: no upgrade check, an existing file is replaced through the recycle bin.
manualImport.loadFailed: The path could not be read.
manualImport.empty: No video file found under this path.
manualImport.noMovieHint: Add the movie to the library first, then pick it here.

oneShot.title: Grab as a one-shot version
oneShot.hint: Creates a version that is grabbed once and never upgraded, next to the existing ones (a Director's Cut, a specific encode), then sends this release to the download client for it.
oneShot.name: Version name
oneShot.nameHint: A short slug: directors-cut, imax, remux-framestor…
oneShot.editionHint: Prefilled from the release; only releases matching it count for this version later.
oneShot.rolledBack: The version was removed again because the grab failed.

mediaManagement.title: Media management
mediaManagement.hint: How finished downloads reach the library: file naming, transfer mode and the recycle bin that receives replaced or deleted files.
mediaManagement.renameFilesHint: Off: files keep the name they had in the download. Existing files can be renamed later from each movie page.
mediaManagement.folderTemplateHint: Applied when a version is created; the folder name is then frozen so files never move silently.
mediaManagement.tokensHint: Radarr syntax: anything between the braces around a token is printed only when the token has a value, so {(Release Year)} disappears without a year. Lower-case tokens print in lower case, {Movie.Title} joins words with dots. {Version} is the version name.
mediaManagement.transferModeHint: A hardlink puts the same bytes under two names: the torrent keeps seeding for free. It needs downloads and the library on one filesystem, at the same path for the client and for Bigarr. Move only makes sense once seeding is over.
mediaManagement.recycleBinPathHint: Replaced and deleted files land here, keeping their path relative to the root folder. Empty: they are deleted for good.
mediaManagement.retentionHint: Files older than this are removed from the bin every hour. 0 keeps them until you empty it yourself.
mediaManagement.importExtraFilesHint: Subtitles and other side files of the release come along with the movie, with the same transfer, named after the movie file with their language. They follow its renames and leave with it on an upgrade or a deletion. Files Bigarr did not import, such as Bazarr's subtitles, are never renamed nor deleted.
mediaManagement.extraFileExtensionsHint: Comma separated, without dots: srt,ass,ssa,sub,idx,sup,vtt. Other extensions (nfo, pdf…) come along under the movie's name; a release's .nfo is kept as .nfo-orig, once, so media servers do not read it as metadata. Video extensions are refused.
mediaManagement.mediaInfoAvailable: ffprobe found at {{path}}: imported files get their codecs, channels, HDR and languages read from the stream.
mediaManagement.mediaInfoMissing: ffprobe was not found: files are imported without media info. Install ffmpeg (the Docker image ships it) or set Bigarr__Media__FfprobePath.
mediaManagement.saveFailed: The settings could not be saved.

wanted.title: Wanted
wanted.hint: Monitored versions without a file, and files below their profile cutoff. The cutoff-unmet task searches them on its own, waiting longer after each empty search; a search from here ignores that wait.
wanted.empty: Nothing is wanted: every monitored version has its file at the cutoff.
wanted.nextSearchHint: When the cutoff-unmet task may search this version again. The wait doubles after each empty search.

blocklist.title: Blocklist
blocklist.hint: Releases refused for a version: failed downloads land here on their own, removals from the queue when you ask. Dropping an entry lets the release be grabbed again.
blocklist.removeFailed: The entry could not be removed.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.hint: Webhooks: every event Bigarr publishes is POSTed as JSON to each endpoint that subscribes to it, in Bigarr's format or Radarr's, for every film or only tagged ones, signed with the secret when there is one, and retried until it lands, restarts included.
notifications.name: Name
notifications.secretHint: Optional. When set, X-Bigarr-Signature carries an HMAC-SHA256 of the body so the receiver can check the origin.
notifications.secretKeepHint: This endpoint is signed. Leave empty to remove the secret, or type a new one.
notifications.allEventsHint: Nothing checked: every event is sent.
notifications.testOk: The endpoint answered HTTP {{status}} in {{ms}} ms.
notifications.testFailed: The endpoint did not accept the test event.
notifications.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Its pending deliveries are dropped.
notifications.removeFailed: The webhook could not be deleted.
notifications.formatBigarrHint: Bigarr's own JSON, { eventType, eventId, occurredAt, instance, data }, with the full snapshot of the film, version, release and file.
notifications.formatRadarrHint: The body Radarr's webhook sends, so tools written for Radarr (Discord bots, Notifiarr, autoscan, autopulse…) work unchanged. A Radarr movie is a version: its id is the one /api/v3/movie gives an API key of the same view.
notifications.viewVersionHint: Only this version of each film is sent; films without it stay silent. View:
notifications.allFilmsHint: Nothing checked: every film is sent.
notifications.someTagsHint: Only films whose versions carry one of the checked tags. Health and test events are always sent.
notifications.noTags: No tag yet. Tags come with Seerr requests and the Radarr import.
notifications.radarrEventsHint: Radarr's format only sends the events Radarr has; the others are greyed out.

health.title: Health
health.allGood: All good: nothing stands in the way of the loop.

tasks.title: Scheduled tasks
tasks.hint: What runs on its own: the RSS pass, the search for missing and upgradable versions, the health check, the maintenance, the weekly backup. Each can be run now.

connect.title: Connect
connect.hint: Bigarr speaks Radarr v3 on /api/v3, so Seerr, Bazarr and Prowlarr plug in as if it were a Radarr. Each connected app gets its own key, and the key decides which version of each film it sees.
connect.name: Name
connect.viewDefault: Default version of each film (a classic Radarr)
connect.viewAll: Every version, one line each (for Bazarr)
connect.viewVersion: One named version only (a Seerr entry for 4K)
connect.versionNameHint: A lowercase slug. Adding a film through this key creates a version of this name; films without it stay invisible to the key.
connect.created: Key created. Copy it now: it is shown only once.
connect.copyFailed: Could not copy; select the text and copy it by hand.
connect.confirmRevoke: Revoke “{{name}}”? The app using it loses access immediately; the key cannot be restored.
connect.noKeys: No key yet. Create one per app you connect.
connect.createFailed: The key could not be created.
connect.revokeFailed: The key could not be revoked.
connect.url: Radarr URL to enter in the app
connect.seerrHint: One Seerr, two Radarr servers on this same URL: a standard server with a version:1080p key and a 4K server with a version:4k key. Each request creates or follows its own version of the film; both servers can share the root folder. Pick the matching quality profile on each.
connect.bazarrHint: One Bazarr per version, like the usual Bazarr + Bazarr 4K pair: a version:1080p key on the first, a version:4k key on the second. Bazarr keeps one line per TMDB id, so a key with the all view would make it skip the second version of a film. Each instance follows its files live over SignalR at /signalr/messages.
connect.prowlarrHint: Add Bigarr as a Radarr application with a default key: Prowlarr pushes its torrent indexers here and keeps them in sync. Only one of Prowlarr push and the read-only Prowlarr sync should be on.

backups.title: Backups
backups.hint: A zip of the database, taken every week and kept four weeks (Bigarr__Backup__IntervalDays, RetentionDays). Restoring stages the file and restarts Bigarr; in Docker the container comes back on the restored database.
backups.createFailed: The backup could not be written.
backups.name: Backup
backups.confirmRestore: Restore “{{name}}”? Everything added since it was taken is lost. Bigarr restarts right away with the restored database; the current one is kept next to it as bigarr.db.before-restore.
backups.restoring: Bigarr is restarting on the restored database. Reload this page in a few seconds.
backups.restoreFailed: The backup could not be restored.
backups.removeFailed: The backup could not be deleted.

importRadarr.title: Import from Radarr
importRadarr.intro: Moves a Radarr library into Bigarr. Each Radarr movie becomes one version of the film, with its monitored flag, quality profile, tags, minimum availability and file. Metadata comes from Radarr itself, so there is no TMDB round trip. The library folders must be reachable from Bigarr under a mapped root folder.
importRadarr.urlHint: Scheme, host and port, with any URL base, e.g. http://radarr:7878.
importRadarr.summary: Radarr {{version}}: {{movies}} movies, {{withFile}} with a file, {{monitored}} monitored, {{already}} already in this library, {{exclusions}} exclusions, {{history}} history lines, {{blocklist}} blocklisted releases, {{customFormats}} custom formats.
importRadarr.versionNameHint: 1080p for a standard Radarr, 4k for a 4K one. A second Radarr imported with another name adds versions to the same films; a film that already has a version with this name gets Radarr's settings instead of a new version.
importRadarr.versionNameInvalid: A version name is a lowercase slug: letters, digits and single dashes.
importRadarr.rootFoldersHint: The Radarr path is read as is on this host when it is reachable; otherwise pick the root folder where the same films live, added on the Library settings page.
importRadarr.noTags: Radarr has no tags in use.
importRadarr.importCustomFormats: Import custom formats and give each mapped profile the scores of its Radarr profile
importRadarr.importHistory: Import history (grabs, imports, failures, deletions, renames of the imported films)
importRadarr.importBlocklist: Import blocklist (releases Radarr rejected for the imported films are not grabbed again)
importRadarr.mappingIncomplete: Map every profile and root folder that has movies, and give a valid version name.

mediaServers.title: Media servers
mediaServers.hint: Bigarr tells each enabled server about imported, upgraded, renamed and deleted files, so it scans just that folder instead of waiting for its own schedule. A server that does not answer is retried a few times; failures show on System → Status.
mediaServers.confirmDelete: Delete “{{name}}”? Bigarr stops telling it about changes; nothing on the server is touched.
mediaServers.removeFailed: The media server could not be deleted.
mediaServers.empty: No media server yet. Add your Plex, Jellyfin or Emby so new files show up right away.
mediaServers.name: Name
mediaServers.urlHint: Scheme, host and port, e.g. http://plex:32400 or http://jellyfin:8096.
mediaServers.tokenHintPlex: The X-Plex-Token of an account that can see this server.
mediaServers.tokenHintApiKey: An API key created in the server's dashboard (Administration → API keys).
mediaServers.pathMappingsHint: Only when the server mounts the library under another path than Bigarr, e.g. /data → /mnt/media.
mediaServers.testFailed: The server did not accept the connection.
